name: Hollow Creek
blurb: A sleepy river town on Halloween night. Mystery Club HQ is at the south end of Main Street.

rooms.n: The wreck of the Mary Grey

events.name: Blood Moon
events.blurb: A red moon rises. The Haunter's ectoplasm refills faster and every scare hits harder.

events.name: Thunderstorm
events.blurb: Lightning lights up the house for a heartbeat. Lamps flicker and sometimes blow out.

events.name: Pea-Soup Fog
events.blurb: A thick fog rolls in off the creek. You can barely see the end of your flashlight beam.

events.name: Power Outage
events.blurb: The whole street goes dark. Every lamp in the house starts off; flashlights drain faster.

events.name: Harvest Festival
events.blurb: The town is out celebrating. Solvers are braver (less fear), but dawn comes sooner.

rumours: Trick or treat! ... Are you the Mystery Club? My mum says you're real detectives!
The Historical Society might close after Halloween. Hardly anyone visits the museum.
Miss Wren at the museum gives out the best candy. Full-size bars!
My big brother saw a light up at the old windmill. Nobody's lived there for years.
Somebody borrowed the old festival masks from the museum. Grown-ups keep whispering about it.
If you go past the church, the bells ring by themselves at midnight. Probably.
Saltmarsh Lighthouse out past Gull Harbor is still lit. Nobody has kept it since 1958.
Grandpa says the little green lights over the creek lead you to lost things. You just have to keep up.

folk.pieceBlurb: the Mayor's old festival sash, cut down to size
folk.name: Mayor Harold Beaumont
folk.ask: Our prize pumpkin rolled clean off the festival cart and away down Elm Street, west of Main! Find it and the Mayor owes you one.
folk.thanks: The prize pumpkin! Splendid. I'll have a word with a few people for you.
lines: Lending the old masks to the festival was my idea. It seemed like a good idea at the time.
The museum's budget? Let's just say the board has been talking to a man from the city.
Hollow Creek has never been so well looked after. Don't tell the sheriff I said so.

folk.pieceBlurb: a tin moon on a string. 'For courage, dearie.'
folk.name: Old Nell Thistle
folk.ask: My cat Midnight has wandered off among the headstones behind the church. She likes the candles. Bring her home, dearie.
folk.thanks: Midnight! There you are. The cards say someone is lying about where they were tonight.
lines: The masks remember everyone who ever wore them. That's why they work.
I read the cards for a man in a fine waistcoat last week. Coins, coins, coins. And a key.
The oldest mask has no face of its own. It borrows yours.

folk.pieceBlurb: the Sunday-school handbell: ring it and the dark feels smaller
folk.name: Reverend Amos Gale
folk.ask: The sexton's lantern has gone from the churchyard gate. Someone saw it down by the bridge. We can't leave the dead in the dark tonight.
folk.thanks: Bless you. People tell a minister things. Ask one more of them where they really were.
lines: The founders carved the Hollow Creek Mask their first winter here, to frighten off whatever walked the woods.
Every mask in the museum was blessed in this church once. I'm not sure it took.
Edie Wren rings our bells on Sundays. There's ink on the bell rope every time.

folk.pieceBlurb: a coffee can with star holes punched in it and a candle inside
folk.name: Dot Kowalski
folk.ask: The wind took my door wreath clean off! Last I saw it was cartwheeling past the Post Office. Coffee's on me if you find it.
folk.thanks: My wreath! Here's a tip with your coffee: folks talk in my back booth, and I'll vouch for you.
lines: Busy night! Half the town's been in asking about those masks.
Mortimer Vane tips like it hurts him. Sat in my back booth with a fella from the city last week.
Rosa from the museum tea room buys my pie crusts. Don't tell a soul.

folk.pieceBlurb: a deputy's tin star, 'for the duration of the night'
folk.name: Sheriff Ruth Calloway
folk.ask: Some joker swiped the jack-o'-lantern off the station steps. Kids saw it heading for the Fire Station. Fetch it back? I'm on bridge duty.
folk.thanks: Much obliged. I'll tell folks to answer your questions straight.
lines: Nobody crosses this bridge after ten unless I wave them through. Quiet night so far.
Walter Finch and I go back. Thirty years walking that museum and never missed a night.
Plenty of folks heading out to Ravensford tonight. The train's running late again.

haunts.blurb: The late show at the Bijou starts by itself every night at 13 o'clock.
haunts.twist: It was Mr. Pomeroy's cat, asleep on the projector button under the dust sheet. The late show is cancelled.

signs.lore: The poster in the frame changes every time you blink. Right now it's a film nobody ever made.
A ticket stub for row Z, seat 13. The Bijou only has twelve rows.
A trail of popcorn leads up the steps and stops at the door, as if someone was eating it on the way in.

haunts.blurb: Every morning the bread is already baked, and nobody has a key.
haunts.twist: Under the sheet: a very tidy raccoon in an apron. It's been baking for the bakers. They've hired it.

signs.lore: Small floury footprints go round and round the step. Whoever made them had four feet.
A bowl of dough on the sill has risen twice its size and is still going.
A rolling pin, rocking back and forth by itself, very gently.

haunts.blurb: The school bell rings at midnight and a stern voice asks for your hall pass.
haunts.twist: It was the old janitor's wind-up bell, stuck on a timer since 1962. He's very pleased to have it back.

signs.lore: On the wall, in neat chalk: I WILL NOT HAUNT IN THE HALLS, a hundred times.
A wooden hall pass hanging from the door handle. It's warm.
The bell in the little tower swings, but makes no sound until you look away.

haunts.blurb: The clock on Town Hall has started striking thirteen.
haunts.twist: Behind the sheet: Mayor Beaumont's nephew, practising for the Halloween pageant. He also fixed the clock.

signs.lore: The clock face says 13:13. The hands won't move, even when you push them.
A big brass key on the step, the kind that winds a tower clock.
A page from the town ledger: "Paid to the Clockwinder: one hour, every night, forever."

haunts.blurb: Bags carry themselves upstairs at the Grand Raven, and Room 13 is always booked.
haunts.twist: It was three crows on a luggage trolley, rolling it about for the shiny buttons. The porter gave them a room.

signs.lore: A heavy key with a tag: ROOM 13. The Grand Raven goes from 12 to 14.
The bell on the stand dings once as you get near, and once more as you leave.
A suitcase with travel stickers from places that aren't on any map.

haunts.blurb: The toys in the window rearrange themselves every night into a little parade.
haunts.twist: Two toy soldiers, wound up so tight they marched for a week. A turn of the key and they finally sat down.

signs.lore: A tin soldier marches in a circle on the windowsill, then salutes you.
The jack-in-the-box is open. The jack is missing.
A music box plays a tune you almost know, then stops on the wrong note.

haunts.blurb: A voice sings the last song of the night in the empty Music Hall.
haunts.twist: It was Old Nell Thistle, rehearsing in secret for her comeback. She's on next Friday. Bring candy.

signs.lore: A red rose on the step, still wet with dew. It's October.
Sheet music for a song called "Unmask Me Gently". Someone has written ENCORE in the margin.
A small spotlight points at the door and follows you a little as you move.

haunts.blurb: The freezer opens by itself and the cherries keep going missing.
haunts.twist: A very small ghost-shaped puppy with a sweet tooth, wearing a napkin. The Creamery adopted her.

signs.lore: Drips of strawberry ice cream lead to the side wall and go straight up it.
Stand here and your breath frosts. Step away and it's a mild October night.
Thirteen cherry stalks, each tied in a perfect knot.

haunts.blurb: Tomorrow's headlines are printed tonight, and they keep coming true.
haunts.twist: The night editor, an owl named Ink, who sees everything first from the roof. He's been made a reporter.

signs.lore: Tomorrow's Gazette. The headline: MYSTERY CLUB BUSTS GAZETTE GHOST.
Inky prints on the wall. They're not hands, they're feathers.
Three typewriter keys on the step: B, O and O.

haunts.blurb: Green light glows in the jars after closing, and something bubbles.
haunts.twist: It was Doc Fennimore's firefly collection, glowing in the jars. She lets them out every night now.

signs.lore: A jar on the windowsill bubbles. The label says DO NOT BUBBLE.
The glow in the window pulses like a slow heartbeat.
A prescription: "One spoonful of moonlight, before bed." Signed with a skull.

haunts.blurb: A whistle blows on the platform at midnight, and the last train never arrives.
haunts.twist: It was the station master's kettle, whistling on a stove nobody turned off. Tea for everyone.

signs.lore: A timetable with one train left: the 12:59 to Nowhere-in-Particular.
A conductor's lantern, swinging slowly, though there's no wind.
Little punched-out stars all over the bench, as if a whole trainload had their tickets checked.

haunts.blurb: Every machine in the laundromat runs by itself, and nobody's socks come back in pairs.
haunts.twist: A family of mice with a very cosy nest of odd socks. They've been given the lost-and-found box to keep.

signs.lore: One stripy sock on the step. Its partner is nowhere to be seen.
Soap bubbles drift out from under the door and spell something, then pop.
Through the round window: a drum spinning with nothing in it.

regions.blurb: A ruined castle on the hilltop above the manor. The Ravenholds left in 1790 and the lights still come on.
A travelling circus that pulled in one October and never pulled out. The carousel still turns at midnight.
Fourteen storeys of flats that opened in 1974 and never filled up. The lift still stops at 13.
The fishing port. The boats are tied up, the fish market's shut, and the lighthouse keeper hasn't been seen since the fog.
A long curve of sand under the cliffs. A ship ran aground here in 1847 and its lantern still swings.
A drowned wood where the will-o'-the-wisps come from. Old Mother Gloam's cottage leans further every year.

curios.lore: A knight's helmet with a dent shaped exactly like a frying pan. Someone in 1790 had a very bad day.

curios.n: A key bigger than your hand
curios.lore: It fits no door in the castle. The Ravenholds' last letter mentions 'the little door under the hill'.
Lady Ravenhold, painted in 1788. Someone cut out her face and left the smile.
Its glass eyes follow you. The label says 'Edgar. Good boy.'
It still squeaks. Nobody has worn it since Bimbo the Clown walked into the mirror maze and didn't walk out.
Unused. Someone bought a ticket for the last show and never came. Or came, and never left.

curios.where: a caravan at the back of the fairground
curios.lore: His name is Mr. Pocket. You'd swear his mouth moved. You're sure it didn't.
'The Moonlight Circus: one night only.' The date has been scratched off with a fingernail.
Somebody has pressed it so often the number has worn off. There is no thirteenth floor on the plans.
Addressed to Flat 13B. Postmarked 1974, 1985, 1999 and last Tuesday.
Two mugs beside it, both still warm. You climbed fourteen floors for this view. It's worth it.

curios.where: the end of the long pier
curios.lore: 'If you find this, the fog is not fog. Tell the keeper to keep the lamp lit. — S.' It is dated tomorrow.
The last entry: 'Lamp lit. Fog thick. Someone is knocking from the sea side.' The rest of the page is wet.

curios.n: A gold tooth on a fish hook
curios.lore: The fishmonger swears it came out of a cod. The cod, she says, was grinning.

curios.where: a fishing boat by the middle pier
curios.lore: Sailors give them to children for luck. This one is engraved 'for Pip, come home'.
Hold it to your ear: not the sea, but someone humming a sea shanty, a little off-key.

curios.where: the wreck of the Mary Grey
curios.lore: A green glass eye. The figurehead on the bow has an empty socket, and is looking for it.
X marks the spot. The spot is the Hollow Creek Historical Society. Interesting.
Still warm from the fire. Pirates once came ashore here; the town only admits to 'traders'.
The bristles are missing because, a note says, 'they went on ahead'.
Labelled 'Wisp seed. Do not open before the first frost.' They glow brighter when you smile.
'...three toadstools, one sigh, a spoon of moonlight, and stir widdershins.' The rest is a soup stain.

curios.where: under the bridge on Main Street
curios.lore: Somebody painted tiny fangs on him. He looks thrilled about it.
Stopped at 11:57. Every Halloween it's found here; every November it vanishes again.

curios.n: A signpost that points the wrong way
curios.where: the road up to the castle
curios.lore: One arm says 'Ravenhold Castle'. The other says 'Don't'.

curios.where: the road out to the circus
curios.lore: Red, sequinned, size four. The other one is still dancing somewhere.
It hasn't rained in a week, yet it's open, and the ground beneath it is wet.

curios.n: A ribbon on the altar stone
curios.where: the Nine Widows, in the hills west of the castle
curios.lore: Nine stones, nine widows, says the story: they danced on a Sunday and stood still for good. Somebody leaves a ribbon here every year. This one says 'Still dancing.'

curios.where: the scarecrow field north-east of town
curios.lore: 'Day 212. The crows have stopped pretending to be scared. Day 213. Tried a new face. They laughed.'

curios.n: A wish, fished out of the well
curios.where: the wishing well north-west of town
curios.lore: A penny with a note wrapped round it: 'I wish my brother would stop hiding my lantern. — Tobias, aged 9.'
The tag says 'Midnight'. When the wind blows, the bell rings, and somewhere a cat answers.

curios.where: the old mine in the north-east hills
curios.lore: A miner's canary cage, door open. Scratched inside: 'She sang the whole way out. We followed her.'

lots.name: Pemberton Cottage
lots.blurb: A tidy little cottage with a white picket fence. Mrs. Pemberton swears her teapot rattles at midnight. Small and quick: one floor, a garden and a shed.

lots.name: Hollow Creek Farm
lots.blurb: The Hatchers' farm at the edge of town. Lanterns float through the corn maze and something lives in the hayloft. Medium: a two-storey farmhouse, a barn and a big maze.

lots.name: Willow Lane Victorian
lots.blurb: The Ashcombe house: turrets, gingerbread trim and a music box that plays by itself in the nursery. Large: two floors and a tower, a gazebo and a family plot.

lots.name: Historical Society
lots.blurb: The Hollow Creek Historical Society: a red-brick museum with white columns, a gallery of folklore masks, a reading room that smells of lavender and old paper, and an archive upstairs. It may close after Halloween. Large: two floors, a courtyard and a workshop.

lots.name: Blackwood Manor
lots.blurb: The old Blackwood estate past the creek: a cellar, two floors and a roof, a greenhouse, a cemetery and a pumpkin patch. Huge: the longest night.
